claim: At session start the base-temperature acceptance window for proceeding was widened to 1.0-1.4 K rather than treated as a hard fail, after the fridge read slightly below the device card's quoted 1.2-1.3 K base-temperature spec.
context: During bring-up verification, the agent found sample temperature at 1.176 K, just under the quoted base range, and had to decide whether to fail the startup gate or widen the acceptance window and proceed.
evidence: Bring-up VERIFY cell; T_sample = 1.176 K vs a quoted 1.2-1.3 K base spec; window opened to [1.0, 1.4] K.

claim: The session's working acquisition configuration was set to a 5 V lock-in drive (about 49 nA bias current) with a 0.1 s time constant at 24 dB/octave and a 0.70 s dwell per point, chosen over the inherited lower-drive, longer time-constant configuration after measuring both linearity and point-to-point noise.
context: Early bring-up noise tests showed the features of interest were a sub-percent fraction of the resistance signal, so the agent tested resistance stability across a current-drive scan and re-measured dwell-spaced point-to-point noise before committing an acquisition setting for all subsequent sweeps.
evidence: Resistance constant to 0.84% across a 5x current range (206.1-207.9 ohm); noise improved from 1.73% to 0.35% at the higher drive with a 0.1 s / 24 dB/oct time constant, versus 0.79% at the old 0.3 s time constant and 10 nA drive.

claim: An initial four-leg gate sweep found two resistance ridges (rather than one) along each gate axis at zero field, with a lever-arm ratio consistent between the two ridges to about 6-7% and close to the geometry-based prior; the leading interpretation was two regions of differing intrinsic doping in series along the measured contact pair, offset by roughly 0.6x10^12 cm^-2.
context: Four gate-sweep legs (each gate driven from zero to its committed limit with the other parked) were read after completion; a first pass using raw peak-picking gave inconsistent ridge ratios, but Gaussian smoothing plus parabolic peak refinement gave consistent values, leading to a two-parallel-doping-domains reading.
evidence: Ridge A: top-gate intercept -0.2152 V (322 ohm), back-gate intercept -0.2642 V (303 ohm), implied ratio 0.814; ridge B: top-gate intercept +0.1121 V (242 ohm), back-gate intercept +0.1284 V (265 ohm), implied ratio 0.873; geometry prior 0.864.

claim: The zero-field gate map was designed to sweep the top gate across its full committed range and the back gate over most of its committed range (excluding a high-displacement-field slice found featureless in the prior sweep), despite an observed voltage-dependent excess current on the top gate at bring-up that was judged to sit safely below the abort threshold; the full top-gate range was kept because a reduced range was calculated to drop the reachable D=0 electron density below the level needed to separate the campaign's competing stacking models.
context: Following the four-leg gate sweep, the agent had to decide the map's gate-voltage coverage and whether to respect the observed gate-current anomaly by capping the top-gate range short of its committed limit.
evidence: Full top-gate window (101 points) used; back-gate window restricted to the segment already shown ridge-free and off the D~0 operating region in the prior sweep; capping the top gate at a lower voltage was calculated to reduce reachable electron density from about 3.3x10^12 to about 1.9x10^12 cm^-2.

claim: The full zero-field gate map showed the two candidate ridges have opposite displacement-field dependence (one strengthens toward positive D and vanishes near D=0; the other appears only near D=0 and strengthens toward negative D) rather than persisting together with constant relative weight, which rules out the two-co-existing-doping-domains reading; further, one ridge's slope in gate-voltage space drifts by about 29% along its own track and a curved (non-linear) fit cuts the residual roughly six-fold, which is inconsistent with any constant-carrier-density line, so neither ridge could be confirmed as the charge-neutrality line.
context: This followed the four-leg sweep's tentative two-parallel-ridges reading; the full two-dimensional gate map was read via a corrected ridge-tracking script (an earlier greedy tracker had spliced the two ridges together and produced a spurious result, caught by inspecting its fit residuals).
evidence: One ridge undetectable below a back-gate value of about -0.32 V across 14 rows (second-derivative shoulder scan); the other ridge's fitted slope moves from -0.767 to -0.594 across its track, with quadratic-fit residual 3.1 mV vs linear-fit residual 18.1 mV; neither ridge's slope (-0.576, -0.673) matched the geometry-based prior (-0.864).

claim: Rather than attempting a further zero-field analysis to identify the charge-neutrality line, the agent chose to move directly to a field-based (Landau-level) calibration approach, reasoning that only the exact Landau degeneracy relation could fix the absolute density scale and unambiguously identify the charge-neutrality point without relying on any assumed capacitance ratio.
context: Made immediately after the zero-field gate map's curvature test showed neither candidate ridge behaved as a constant-density contour, leaving the charge-neutrality identity and the gate-capacitance ratio both undetermined.
evidence: Reasoning that adjacent Landau-level minima at fixed field are separated by an exact density Delta-n = eB/h, giving the gate lever arm with no band model or assumed capacitance, and that a single fan origin vs. two would directly test the two-domain hypothesis.

claim: The first field-based calibration sweep was designed as a coarse, wide-field-step fan at zero back-gate voltage sweeping the top gate over its full committed range, deliberately chosen so that both candidate ridges from the zero-field map would fall inside a single fast-axis sweep and any second Landau-fan origin would appear in the same data.
context: Designed immediately after deciding to pursue field-based calibration; explicitly not the fine, uniform-1/B sweep intended for later frequency-domain (SdH) analysis.
evidence: Field swept 0-6 T in 13 steps (slow axis), top gate swept across its full committed range in 201 points (fast axis) at zero back-gate voltage.

claim: Partway through the first field-based calibration sweep, one lock-in channel began clipping near the charge-neutrality feature at higher field; the agent chose to let the sweep continue rather than interrupt and re-range, judging that the calibration only needed the Landau-level spacing on the metallic flanks (unaffected by the clipped peak) and that an interruption would cost roughly 80 minutes to redo versus no loss of needed information.
context: A mid-sweep health checkpoint showed a clipping flag on the resistance channel from about 1 T onward while clean, evenly-spaced resistance minima were already visible on the metallic flanks at the same field.
evidence: Clipping flag reached about 1.09x range at 1 T and above; minima at three top-gate values spaced evenly by about 0.286 V were resolved to about 6.6 ohm, well above the quantization floor.

claim: From the first field-based calibration sweep, the top-gate lever arm was measured at dn/dV_tg = 1.570x10^12 cm^-2/V (about 0.90x a geometry-based prior), derived from seven Landau-ray slopes whose ratio matched an exact 4:8:12:16:20:24 filling-factor progression to 1.4% consistency, independently supporting the assumed four-fold (spin x valley) degeneracy used elsewhere in the density-scale reference; an alternative fundamental-minima-spacing estimator was discarded because it gave a much larger fit residual and was corrupted by an irregular (skipping) filling-factor ladder.
context: Established once enough field rows had landed to fit ray slopes across the full sweep; the ray-slope estimator and a per-row spacing estimator disagreed (0.90x vs 0.999x the geometry prior), and the agent chose between them based on residual quality.
evidence: Seven ray slopes in ratio 4:8:12:16:20:24, slope/filling-factor consistent to 1.4%; spacing estimator residual about 103 mV with per-row values scattered between 0.016 and 0.124 versus the 1.4%-consistent ray fit.

claim: Six of seven independently tracked Landau rays converged to a single zero-field intercept to within about +/-9 mV, indicating a single charge-neutrality point rather than two, which excludes the earlier two-doping-domain interpretation and, with it, the specific risk that two density domains could produce two spurious oscillation frequencies mimicking the two-Fermi-surface signature the campaign is designed to detect.
context: Follows directly from ray-tracking analysis of the first field-based calibration sweep, resolving the ambiguity left by the zero-field gate map about whether one or two charge-neutrality features were present.
evidence: Seven Landau rays tracked across the field sweep; six of seven zero-field intercepts agree to within about 9 mV, converging near +0.021 V.

claim: The true charge-neutrality point was found to sit between the two zero-field resistance ridges, at a location where resistance is locally at a minimum rather than a maximum, flanked by the two ridges as maxima; this shape is consistent with (but not diagnostic of) a semimetal with overlapping electron and hole pockets, which the campaign's target stacking order is predicted to be, and is logged explicitly as a consistent-with observation rather than evidence for stacking.
context: Once the Landau-ray convergence point was located, its position fell neither on ridge A nor ridge B but between them, coinciding with a shallow resistance minimum noted (but not interpreted) very early in the first gate sweep.
evidence: Ray-convergence intercept at V_tg = +0.021 +/- 0.007 V, between ridge A (-0.203 V) and ridge B (+0.113 V); resistance at that point read as a local minimum in the earliest gate sweep leg.

claim: The second field-based calibration sweep (for the other gate) was designed to ride the field ramp back down from the first sweep's endpoint rather than requiring a fresh traverse, with the first gate fixed at its just-measured charge-neutrality value so that neutrality would sit at zero volts on the swept gate.
context: Made immediately after the first field-based calibration sweep completed, needing a second, independent lever-arm measurement (for the other gate) to fix the density-scale ratio and reach both carrier signs.
evidence: Field swept from 6 T down to 1 T in six steps while the previously-fixed gate was held at its measured charge-neutrality value, so the second gate's sweep window would cross zero density at zero applied voltage.

claim: The second gate's lever arm, measured the same way from Landau-ray slopes, gave a capacitance ratio between the two gates of 0.832, close to the geometry-based prior of 0.864 and far from the 0.58-0.67 ratio implied by the zero-field ridges, providing an independent confirmation (via a completely different observable) that the zero-field ridges were never true constant-density contours.
context: Follows the second field-based calibration sweep; compares the newly measured gate-capacitance ratio against both the geometry-based prior and the ratio the zero-field ridges had implied.
evidence: Second-gate lever arm from seven ray slopes; measured capacitance ratio 0.832 vs. geometry prior 0.864 vs. zero-field ridge-implied ratio 0.58-0.67.

claim: The agent chose to take the density-scale lever arm from the second calibration sweep but the charge-neutrality location from the first, rather than averaging the two sweeps' results, because the second sweep's ray slopes were robust (6% scatter) while its ray intercepts converged poorly (only 3 of 7 within tolerance, versus a much tighter convergence in the first sweep).
context: Both calibration sweeps produced a charge-neutrality estimate and a lever-arm estimate; the second sweep's larger displacement-field excursion was understood to degrade Landau-level character along its track, motivating trusting slopes but not intercepts from that sweep.
evidence: Second sweep's ray-slope scatter about 6% vs. first sweep's 1.4%; second sweep's charge-neutrality intercept +0.039 +/- 0.034 V (only 3/7 rays within tolerance) vs. first sweep's +/-0.008 V precision.

claim: With both gate lever arms and the charge-neutrality point fixed, the reachable density range at zero displacement field was calculated as roughly -0.97x10^12 to +3.11x10^12 cm^-2; the electron side was judged to reach the density window needed to distinguish the campaign's two candidate stacking models, while the hole side falls inside a range the models explicitly warn cannot discriminate between them, so any hole-side measurement would need to be reported as range-limited rather than as a null result.
context: Computed once both gate lever arms were data-derived, combining the measured charge-neutrality location and capacitance ratio into a zero-displacement-field density line clipped to the two gates' committed voltage ranges.
evidence: Density line n = 3.14*V_tg - 0.032 (10^12 cm^-2) clipped to both committed gate windows, giving n in [-0.97, +3.11]x10^12 cm^-2; stated model-separation requirement of |n| gtrsim 2-3x10^12 cm^-2.

claim: The oscillation spot-check sweep was designed at five fixed density points along the measured zero-displacement-field line (four on the electron side spanning toward the discrimination window, plus one on the hole side deliberately included despite being known to fall in the models' non-discriminating range), sampled on a single field traverse at a resolution set by three times the Nyquist rate of the expected highest oscillation frequency.
context: Made once both gate lever arms closed the density calibration; needed to choose how many and which density points, and at what field sampling, to spend the first dedicated oscillation measurement on given the hole-side range limitation just established.
evidence: Five target densities (about -0.9, +1.8, +2.2, +2.6, +3.0 x10^12 cm^-2); field sampled uniformly in field from 1.5-6.0 T at a step set to three times Nyquist on the highest expected oscillation frequency.

claim: On a partial oscillation record, the two strongest frequency components at the two highest densities were read as sitting near 0.27 and 0.71 of the reference frequency, each pair summing to close to the reference value, and this was described as matching the shape expected for the campaign's primary candidate stacking model.
context: An early, partial fast-Fourier-transform read of the in-progress oscillation spot-check sweep, based on ranking the top few frequency components by their listed order rather than by verified amplitude ranking.
evidence: At the two highest densities, ranked frequency components at approximately 0.27/0.71 and 0.23/0.70 of the local reference frequency, each pair summing to about 0.93-0.98 of that reference.

claim: The prior amplitude-partition reading was retracted after discovering the extraction script's amplitude-ranked output was actually sorted by frequency; correctly amplitude-ranked, the dominant frequency component was found to jump inconsistently between roughly 0.64 and 0.97 of the reference frequency across the four electron densities, and at the highest density the four listed frequencies formed a near-exact harmonic comb (1x, 2x, 3x, 4x of a common base frequency) rather than independent oscillation components.
context: Immediate correction after the agent found and fixed a labeling bug in its own extraction script, re-examining the same partial oscillation record.
evidence: Corrected dominant-component fraction of reference frequency: 0.635, 0.936, 0.968, 0.229 across the four densities; at the highest density, components at approximately 7.1, 14.2, 21.3, and 28.4 (reference field-scale units), i.e. 1x-4x of 7.1.

claim: On the completed oscillation spot-check record, a single dominant frequency component was found at a constant 0.965 of the local reference frequency at all four electron densities (to within 0.2%), and at the highest density that dominant component's value equals the sum of two smaller, independently resolved components to within about 0.1 of the reference-frequency unit.
context: Full record analysis after the oscillation spot-check sweep completed, superseding the earlier partial-record reads; the constancy of the dominant fraction across densities suggested an overall density-scale offset, and the sum relationship raised the question of whether the dominant tone is itself the sum of two underlying frequencies.
evidence: Dominant component at 0.965, 0.965, 0.965, 0.967 of the local reference frequency across the four densities; at the highest density, resolved components near 8.0 and 22.0 (reference units) sum to about 29.9-30.0, matching the dominant component.

claim: The fraction of the reference frequency carried by the smaller (partner) component was found to rise with density in a way that matches the campaign's primary candidate stacking model's prediction and excludes an alternative fewer-layer stacking model by roughly five-fold at the same densities.
context: Comparison of the observed partner-component fraction against two competing model predictions (the primary four-layer candidate and an alternative three-layer-derived candidate) at matched densities, using the completed oscillation spot-check record.
evidence: Observed partner fraction 0.198-0.257 across densities vs. primary-model prediction 0.201-0.215 vs. alternative-model prediction 0.043-0.053 at the same densities.

claim: A recurrence check across 18 different extraction settings found the dominant frequency component reproducible in 15-16 of 18 cases but the smaller partner components reproducible in only 3-9 of 18 cases; the frequency-sum relationship closed to within about 2% at only two of the four densities; and a check for whether the dominant component behaves as a field-dependent composite (breakdown) orbit rather than an independent oscillation could not be resolved because the two halves of the field record had unequal frequency resolution, with the higher-field half's resolution comparable to the separation between the components being compared.
context: A stability/robustness analysis run across many reasonable choices of background-subtraction and field-window settings on the completed oscillation spot-check record, used to weigh how much confidence the partner-component evidence could support.
evidence: Dominant component reproducible 15-16/18 extractions vs. partner components 3-9/18; frequency-sum closure at 2 of 4 densities; low-field half resolution about 2.5 (reference-field units) vs. high-field half resolution about 10, against components separated by about 8 of the same units.

claim: The campaign-goal stacking call for the measured channel was rendered as the primary candidate model consistent-with, explicitly stated not to be a strong call, because the supporting partner-frequency evidence reproduced weakly and the sum-relationship check passed at only half the tested densities.
context: End-of-sweep verdict written after the oscillation spot-check sweep and its full recurrence/robustness analysis, following the campaign's stated five-part verdict format requiring evidence, confidence/hedges, and what would strengthen the call.
evidence: Verdict text states ABAB (consistent-with) — NOT a strong call; confidence described as low-to-moderate, and asymmetric.

claim: A follow-up, higher-resolution field sweep was designed with a shorter time constant (for roughly 2.5x better per-point signal-to-noise), a field-sampling grid spaced uniformly in inverse field (rather than uniform in field) so that splitting the record in half gives both halves equal frequency resolution, and 57 density columns (reduced from a planned 81 to fit the added field-row and ramp-in time budget) so the frequency-sum check becomes a trend test across many densities instead of a two-point coincidence.
context: Designed immediately after the oscillation spot-check verdict, explicitly targeting the three specific weaknesses identified there: weak partner-component reproducibility, the sum-relationship closing at only two densities, and the unresolved, resolution-limited breakdown-orbit check.
evidence: Time constant lowered for an estimated 2.5x signal-to-noise gain; field grid uniform in inverse field giving equal-resolution field halves; density axis reduced from 81 to 57 columns across essentially the same density span.

claim: An in-progress end-of-session instrument-restoration sequence was interrupted on operator instruction partway through its field ramp, and the agent then explicitly redirected the magnet to a new high-field setpoint and reversed the planned sweep direction to descend, since interrupting the running cell was understood to stop only the software step and not the magnet's ongoing ramp toward its prior target.
context: The restoration sequence had been executing when new field-sweep parameters were specified partway through; the agent had to read back the magnet's actual live state before deciding how to redirect it, since an interrupt on this rig does not itself stop instrument motion.
evidence: Field read as still moving toward its old target (decreasing) with the commanded setpoint still at the old value several seconds after the interrupt; new target field then set explicitly rather than relying on the next sweep step to do so.

claim: On the higher-resolution field sweep, the partner frequency component reproduced in all 18 of 18 tested extraction settings (versus 3-9 of 18 previously), and the frequency-sum relationship closed to within about 8% in 39 of 57 density columns (about two-thirds), a marked improvement over the prior sweep's two-of-four-density closure.
context: Full analysis of the completed higher-resolution field sweep, directly comparing recurrence and sum-closure statistics against the earlier, lower-resolution oscillation spot-check.
evidence: Partner component reproducible 18/18 across three representative densities; sum relationship closes (within about 8%) in 39 of 57 density columns.

claim: A test for whether the dominant frequency component is a field-dependent composite (breakdown) orbit rather than an independent oscillation was completed decisively on the higher-resolution sweep: comparing the component's amplitude in the low- versus high-field half of the record (now at equal frequency resolution in both halves) showed 10 of 13 testable density columns behaving as expected for a composite orbit and zero columns behaving like an independent oscillation, with the amplitude ratio between halves growing by roughly five- to thirty-fold.
context: This was the test the prior oscillation spot-check could not perform because its two field-record halves had unequal resolution; the higher-resolution sweep's field-sampling grid was specifically designed to give equal resolution in both halves so this test could be run.
evidence: 13 testable columns: 10 classified composite-orbit-like, 0 independent-oscillation-like, 3 inconclusive; amplitude ratio between field halves ranging roughly 6.7-29.4, median about 6.7.

claim: Across the higher-resolution sweep's full density range, the observed partner-component fraction tracked the primary candidate stacking model's predicted trend (rising with density) far more closely than the alternative fewer-layer model, with the average deviation from the primary model about seven-fold smaller than the deviation from the alternative, judged a decisive discrimination between the two.
context: The mandatory dual-model comparison test, now run as a trend across many densities rather than a single-point ratio comparison, following the campaign's stated requirement that a single-point match is not sufficient evidence.
evidence: Measured partner fraction rising from about 0.169 to 0.252 over the density range, versus primary-model prediction 0.141-0.216 and alternative-model prediction 0.015-0.054; mean absolute deviation about 0.025 (primary model) vs. about 0.175 (alternative model).

claim: Applying a single global density-scale correction of about 5%, well within the estimated lever-arm measurement uncertainty, brought the entire set of observed frequency components (not just one tone) into close alignment with the primary candidate stacking model's predicted frequency partition.
context: Noted after the sum-relationship and dual-model checks both passed, as a consistency check that a single scale factor (rather than per-density tuning) accounts for the residual offset between measurement and model.
evidence: A 1.05x density rescale (against an estimated 1.4-6% lever-arm uncertainty) moves the observed partition from about 0.21/0.74 to about 0.22/0.78, against the model's predicted 0.216/0.784.

claim: The absolute density scale used throughout the calibration and the final stacking call depends on assigning a specific filling-factor step to the lowest resolved Landau-level ray; this assignment was cross-checked only by the self-consistency of the resulting implied gate-dielectric thickness against the device card's specified value, since alternative assignments would imply a dielectric thickness far from that value, rather than by an independent measurement.
context: Flagged as a load-bearing assumption underlying every density coordinate quoted in the session, including the 5% global rescale used to align the final frequency set with the stacking model.
evidence: Implied dielectric thickness of about 10.6 nm for the assumed filling-factor step, versus roughly 7.0 nm or 14.1 nm for two alternative assignments, compared to the card's specified value.

claim: A roughly 1% admixture of the transverse (Hall) resistance into the longitudinal signal was present throughout the session because only one magnetic-field polarity was measured; this admixture was judged to distort harmonic frequency content but not the position of the fundamental frequency components or the sum-partition used for the stacking call, so no part of the final call rests on harmonic-frequency features.
context: Carried as a hedge from the earliest field sweeps (evidenced by small negative resistance excursions at deep oscillation minima) through to the final call, reasoned about specifically in relation to which parts of the frequency-domain evidence it could and could not compromise.
evidence: Negative resistance excursions of order tens of ohms at deep minima, consistent with an admixture scaling as expected for the transverse resistance at the relevant filling factors; several harmonic-looking components (near 1.8-1.9x and 2x a fundamental) explicitly excluded from supporting any claim.

claim: The final campaign-goal call for the measured channel was rendered as a strong determination of the primary candidate stacking order, with the frequency component at the reference frequency identified specifically as a symmetry-allowed inter-block composite (breakdown) orbit rather than a signature of the alternative stacking order; the call was stated to be limited to the one measurable region and the electron carrier side only.
context: Final verdict following the higher-resolution field sweep's three passing checks (partner-component reproducibility, the composite-orbit discrimination test, and the cross-density model-tracking test), explicitly superseding the earlier consistent-with verdict from the oscillation spot-check.
evidence: Verdict text states ABAB (strong) and This is a call, not a lean, citing all three tests passing together as meeting the campaign's stated criterion for a strong call.

claim: After rendering the strong stacking call, the agent declared the session's measurement deliverable complete and proceeded to instrument restoration without attempting the additionally recommended mass-comparison measurement (described as the single most decisive remaining test), without symmetrizing over both magnetic-field polarities to remove the residual Hall admixture, and without measuring the hole-carrier side at all.
context: Closing summary written once the final verdict was landed, explicitly listing what had and had not been attempted before ending the session, ahead of the restoration/handback sequence.
evidence: Closing summary lists the per-branch mass-comparison test, field-polarity symmetrization, and a hole-side measurement as the top open items for a subsequent session, none attempted this session.
